title: Path claims, work lanes and collisions
situations: Two items need the same file.
Implementation discovers an additional required file.
A claim/boundary refusal stops an otherwise necessary change.
A merged item waits for delivery while other items need its former files.
A landed item reopens for a correction and needs fresh claims before editing.
An ordering condition is satisfied while the upstream path claim is still active.
current: Source behavior: required-per-task readiness defers before generated tasks exist, then reports uncovered paths from the same task coverage evaluator used by claim gates. Whole-item claims do not substitute for task bindings; regressions cover pre-task, missing and partial coverage. Source now releases item-owned claims at recorded landing, exposes holder-only release and cancel commands, and requires fresh coverage for rework; live rollout proof remains pending. Per-task coverage counts tasks whose coverage was released at landing as covered, so a reopened Epic claims only its rework touch set on the landed task it changes, while unlanded tasks keep full File Budget coverage. After landing, the merge boundary and the selected Dash path-claims done gate both check touched files against the claims released at that landing; open rework claims replace that coverage. Satisfied dependency ordering now contributes effective coordination without rewriting its stored edge; other unmet conditions keep serialization.
questions: Overlap procedure and current override source were inspected, but collision/authorization scenarios were not executed.
Verify each scope expansion/refusal routes to current registered commands and never recommends dropping required work.
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.
